newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan investors to raise bond weighting in July.
newsitem.headline: Japan investors to raise bond weighting in July.

text.p: Japanese institutional investors are set to increase investments in bonds while scaling back on stocks and cash, a Reuters investment survey showed on Friday.

However, following the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) "tankan" survey of corporate sentiment earlier this week, investors said they must consider possible gyrations on financial markets if Japan raises its interest rates.
The tankan for June showed big Japanese manufacturers in surprisingly upbeat mood.

In the Reuters monthly Global Asset Allocation survey, which asked 15 Japan-based financial institutions in late June about their investment strategy for July, the average overall portfolio weighting for bonds rose 0.59 percentage point to 39.09 percent from the previous month's survey.
The weighting for bonds rose for the first time since December 1996.
Meanwhile, the average overall weighting for equities declined 0.26 percentage points to 46.82 percent.
The average weighting for cash also fell 0.33 percentage point to 14.09 percent.
As for equities, investors plan to step up their investments in Germany, Japan, Britain and emerging markets. The weighting of German and Japanese equities showed particularly large increases.
The weighting for the Japanese stock market rose sharply by 1.69 percentage points to 26.67 percent. It has risen by 3.57 percentage points over the last four months.
Investors expect the Japanese stock market in July to move in a relatively narrow range with a lower floor than the previous month.
The investors expect the Nikkei stock average to move between 19,500 points and 21,500 points.
Nevertheless, they said the supply-and-demand conditions will likely be tight amid an inflow of money from public pension funds.

The Japanese market has also grown more attractive in comparison with other Asian markets as Japanese corporations show robust earnings and worries about the possibility of a financial system crisis have subsided.
Moreover, the stronger yen against the dollar made the yen assets more appealing for dollar-based foreign investors.
Investors also raised the weighting of German equities by an average of 0.38 percentage point to 7.33 percent, the third highest level since the survey started in June 1994.
The weak mark, low interest rates and companies' restructuring efforts will likely continue to buoy German corporate earnings through 1997, Nikko Research Centre said.

On the United States and Canada, investors lowered their weighting by an average of 1.12 percentage points to 39.41 percent. The weighting on U.S. and Canadian stocks fell below 40 percent for the first time since November 1996.
Most investors surveyed do not expect that the U.S. Federal Reserve to raise interest rates at the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on July 1 and 2.
"A number of valuations, such as price-earning ratios and dividend yields, show that the level of U.S. stock prices is too high," said Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
In bond markets, the weighting for the Japanese market rose for the second consecutive month to 16.44 percent, up sharply by 2.26 percentage points.
Although investors are worried about a possible interest rate increase, they raised the weighting to avoid foreign exchange risk amid the yen's rise against the dollar.
The weighting for U.S. bonds declined for the fourth consecutive month to 37.95 percent, down 0.70 percentage point.

Investors were concerned that foreign investors, including central banks, which have a rather large weighting for U.S. bonds in their portfolios, could start to sell as the dollar remains capped against other currencies.
The weighting for British bonds increased for the fifth consecutive month to 8.93 percent, up one percentage point, while those for all other European bond markets declined.
